text.p: These are the leading stories in Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonian parliament adopted on Thursday new law on languages of national minorities at Skopje teachers' academy.

- Macedonian Deputy Prime Minister Jane Miljovski said the best way for Macedonia to receive aid from EU is in form of grant. Macedonia is burdened by obligation to pay back $85 million to European Investment Bank, he said.

- Bulgarian President Petar Stojanov told paper that dialogue between Macedonia and Bulgaria is necessary on outstanding issues. Together the two countries can achieve all goals and help each other, he said.

- Macedonia proposed five projects at SECI initiative meeting in Geneva, Macedonian Development Minister Abduleman Badjeti told reporters Thursday. Macedonia is interested in construction of railway to Bulgaria and several roads in Macedonia that are within scope of east-west project.

- State Departement said in report on human rights in Macedonia that Macedonian government mostly respected citizens' rights, citing as problems police harassment and discrimination of women. National minorities should be more represented in government administration, the report says.
